land.text: al-Andalus, the Iberian rump of the Umayyad realm after the Abbasid revolution (Cliopatria's last Umayyad shape equals its first Córdoba shape)

predecessors.note: The Emirate page: Abd al-Rahman 'established an independent emirate in southern Iberia in 756'; the Abd al-Rahman I page: 'Reign: 14 May 756 - 30 September 788', Seville taken 'without violence' by March 756.

land.text: the same state: Abd al-Rahman III declared himself caliph 'on 16 January 929'; Cliopatria's Caliphate row begins in 936

successors.note: The Emirate and the Caliphate are one Umayyad state under a new title; Cliopatria keeps two rows with different Wikidata ids (Q1337854, Q171740), the caliphate-of-cordoba dossier is written by another group, which should treat 929 as a rename. Toledo (surrendered 2 August 932), Badajoz (930) and Zaragoza (937) came back after 929 (Abd al-Rahman III page).

capitals.name: Córdoba
capitals.note: The Emirate page names Córdoba as the capital in its text; the infobox extract gave no capital. Madinat al-Zahra, begun by Abd al-Rahman III, is outside this span's evidence.

rulers.name: Abd al-Rahman III
rulers.title: emir; caliph from 16 January 929
rulers.note: 'Abd al-Rahman succeeded Abdallah the day after his death, 16 October 912.'

correction.text: Córdoba and Seville, the south taken by Abd al-Rahman I in 756

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 756 only: the founding core. The Emirate page says the 'first unification of al-Andalus (including Toledo, Zaragoza, Pamplona, and Barcelona) still took more than twenty-five years to complete'; Seville fell 'by March 756' (Abd al-Rahman I page). Cliopatria draws the whole of al-Andalus from 757; the pages opened do not date when Toledo, the Upper March or Barcelona were brought in, so 757 stands (conf 1 for those lands). [Repair eu-12-a, 2026-10-25: the ledger now bridges 756 to 757 with a confidence-1 gain from the Fihrid governors; the Abd al-Rahman I page says most of central and northern al-Andalus stayed outside the emir's rule until 779, so the 757 shape is Cliopatria's reading for those lands.]

correction.text: 757-758 as drawn; from 759 without Septimania (Narbonne, Roussillon)

keyframe_review.note: 757-762, 445,142 km2, bbox north to 43.60 N. The shape holds Septimania, which the Septimania page ends in 759 ('Narbonne capitulated to the Christian Franks in 759'; 'The region of Roussillon was taken by the Franks in 760'); Cliopatria drops it only in 763 (48 cells, centred 42.8 N, 2.4 E). Valid as drawn for 757-758; from 759 without Septimania. No infobox area on the Emirate page. The 756-757 step is the ledger's confidence-1 gain of 757 (Yusuf al-Fihri's lands).
763-767, 434,914 km2: Septimania gone (759). The Abbasid governor al-Ala's army is defeated at Carmona in 763 ('By 763 Abd al-Rahman had to get back to the business of war'); no border moved.
768-771, 434,697 km2: two cells change at the Pyrenean edge; nothing in the pages opened explains them (unverified: page budget).

772-777, 434,626 km2: the shape before the 778 Upper March revolt; Toledo, Zaragoza and Barcelona are drawn in although the Emirate page says the unification 'took more than twenty-five years' (conf 1).

778-782, 406,149 km2: 110 cells (Zaragoza, Huesca, Lleida; centred 42.0 N, 0.7 E) are removed. The Septimania page: 'When Charlemagne invaded the Upper March in 778'; the Abd al-Rahman I page has al-Husayn 'declaring independence' at Zaragoza in 781 and the emir's army advancing on it by 783 (the same page also says Zaragoza submitted in 779). The shape matches the loss of the Upper March. [Repair eu-12-a: 53 of the 110 cells are in Cliopatria's Frankish shape (ledger 778, confidence 1, mirroring kingdom-of-the-franks /ledger/59); the rest are the rebel lords' (ledger 778).]

783-787, 434,626 km2: the Upper March is back ('By 783 Abd al-Rahman's army advanced on Zaragoza', Abd al-Rahman I page); identical to the 772 shape. Girona is still in the shape although 'In 785 the county of Girona (with Besalú) to the south of the Pyrenees was taken' (Spanish March page, ledger 785): valid for 783-784, from 785 without Girona (the 788 shape drops it).

correction.text: 783-784 as drawn; from 785 without the county of Girona with Besalú

keyframe_review.note: 788-792, 429,712 km2: the county of Girona (with Besalú) is lost. 'In 785 the county of Girona (with Besalú) to the south of the Pyrenees was taken'; Cliopatria shows it three years late.

793-799, 428,052 km2: small changes at the Pyrenean edge (three cells added, eight removed); the pages dated the Frankish overlordship of the upper Ebro to 794 but name no land (unverified: page budget).

correction.text: 801-805 without Barcelona, which Louis the Pious took in 801

keyframe_review.note: 800-805, 422,747 km2: the Urgell and Cerdanya cells are already out ('Urgell and Cerdanya were added in 798'), but Barcelona is still in; 'Louis the Pious took Barcelona from its Moorish ruler in 801'. Cliopatria shows the loss in 806.

806-813, 414,004 km2: 37 cells go in 806, Barcelona (14 cells) and a belt in Navarre and Huesca (23 cells). The Navarre page: Franks 'in 806 took Navarre under their protection'; the Spanish March page has Pamplona under Frankish overlordship in 798 and the upper Ebro in 794.
814-824, 413,265 km2: three cells lost on the Huesca and Navarre edge against 806; 816 'defeated by the Moors in the 816 Battle of Pancorbo' (Spanish March page) moved no border.

825-869, 412,446 km2: five cells at the north-western Duero fringe go in 825, the year the Alfonso II page dates the start of the repopulation of 'parts of Galicia, León, and Castile'. The Emirate had never held that belt in earnest (the Duero was the 'Desert of the Duero'); the shape stands. The Emirate page gives no area to compare.

870-874, 411,485 km2: three cells at Porto go in 868 ('Count Vimara Perez in 868 conquered Porto and resettled the district'). [Repair eu-12-a, 2026-10-25: 'In January 872, Isma'il ibn Musa entered Zaragoza ... the two of them together taking Monzon' and 'Furtun ibn Musa occupied Tudela' (Banu Qasi page); the shape keeps them although banu-qasi /ledger/0 founds the Banu Qasi state on them in 872 (emirate ledger 872).]

correction.text: 870-871 as drawn; from 872 without Zaragoza, Monzón and Tudela, taken by the Banu Qasi

keyframe_review.note: 875-877, 411,509 km2: one cell added on the Huesca edge; the war with Alfonso III begins ('Fighting occurred almost constantly between 875 and 883'). [Repair eu-12-a: the same 872 loss to the Banu Qasi as in the previous keyframe.]

correction.text: 875-877 without Zaragoza, Monzón and Tudela (Banu Qasi from 872)

minus.text: Reyyo (Bobastro), Elvira (Granada) and Jaén, the lands of Umar ibn Hafsun, with Monzón and Tudela, Banu Qasi land

correction.text: 878-882 as drawn without Zaragoza, Monzón and Tudela (Banu Qasi from 872); from 883 also without Reyyo, Elvira and Jaén; Zaragoza returns in 884 and Tudela and Monzón stay out, so this is the shape of 884-897

keyframe_review.note: 878-897, 406,938 km2: 17 cells south of the Douro (Viseu, Aveiro, Coimbra) go in 878-879 (Alfonso III page). From 883 the shape also holds the rebel south: 'By 883, he had become the leader of the rebels in the provinces to the south and the west of the' capital (Ibn Hafsun page), who held Reyyo (Bobastro), Elvira (Granada) and Jaén (Abdallah page). Valid for 878-882; from 883 without the rebel provinces. [Repair eu-12-a, 2026-10-25: Zaragoza, Monzón and Tudela are out from 872 (Banu Qasi page); Zaragoza returns in 884 ('the emir ... took Zaragoza'), Tudela and Monzón do not.]

correction.text: from c. 900: the vicinity of Córdoba plus the Banu Qasi march of Tudela and Tarazona, the rest held by rebels and local lords

keyframe_review.note: 898-910, 406,844 km2. The Emirate page: 'the power of emir Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Umawi (c. 900) did not extend beyond Córdoba itself'; the Abd al-Rahman III page says of 912 'He inherited an emirate on the verge of dissolution, his power extending not far beyond the vicinity of Córdoba'. Nominal overlordship went on (898: Lubb ibn Muhammad of the Banu Qasi 'recognizes Emir Abd Allah in exchange for the governorship of Tudela and Tarazona'). Drawn from c. 900 as the vicinity of Córdoba with the Banu Qasi march as a vassal; the radius is a reading (conf 2). [Repair eu-12-a: the ledger loss is dated 898 with 'c. 900' noted, so that it agrees with this keyframe's first year.]

correction.text: the vicinity of Córdoba, the Banu Qasi march of Tudela and Tarazona, and the Balearic Islands (903)

keyframe_review.note: 911-921, 408,419 km2, bbox east to 4.30 E: the Balearic Islands are added (the Balearic page dates the conquest to 903: 'In 903, the Muslims under the Arab Commander Issam al-Khawlani defeated the Franks and captured the Balearic Islands'). Until the reconquests of 913-922 the emirate is the vicinity of Córdoba with the Balearics; the ledger then adds Écija and Seville (913), Málaga to Algeciras (914), Valencia (915), Guadix, Jerez and Cádiz (921) and Pechina (922). Cliopatria's removal of 21 Soria and Burgos cells in 911 is not explained by the pages (conf 1).

correction.text: without Toledo, Badajoz and the Upper March, not yet reduced

keyframe_review.note: 922-925, 408,300 km2. The Emirate page: 'Abd al-Rahman III rapidly restored Umayyad power throughout al-Andalus'; the Abd al-Rahman III page dates Badajoz to 930 and Toledo to 2 August 932 and turns to Zaragoza's governor without a date; those lands (and the Upper March of the Banu Qasi and Tujibids) are removed here and belong to the Caliphate of Córdoba's years. The rest of the Cliopatria shape rests on the undated 'throughout al-Andalus' (conf 1 in the ledger).

correction.text: 926-929: as 922, with the Hafsunid south back; Toledo, Badajoz and the Upper March still outside

keyframe_review.note: 926-935, 408,133 km2, but the emirate ends in January 929 with the proclamation of the Caliphate, so the shape is used for 926-929 only; 930-935 belong to the caliphate-of-cordoba dossier. In 928 Bobastro surrenders and the Hafsunid south returns ('Hafs ... surrendered in 928').

ledger.note: 756: Abd al-Rahman I founds the Emirate of Córdoba. 'Established an independent emirate in southern Iberia in 756'; reign from 14 May 756 after landing at Almuñécar in September 755 and taking Seville 'without violence' by March 756. The core is Córdoba and Seville; the rest of al-Andalus followed over 'more than twenty-five years'. [Reviewer eu-12-a, 2026-10-25: counterpart changed from umayyad-caliphate, which the umayyad-caliphate dossier ends in 750, handing al-Andalus to the 'Fihrid governors of al-Andalus' (its /ledger/93).]

region.text: the rest of al-Andalus as Cliopatria draws it from 757: Toledo and the centre, the Upper March, Barcelona and Septimania, beyond the Córdoba and Seville core

ledger.note: 757: the rest of Cliopatria's 757 al-Andalus (445,142 km2) passes to the emir from Yusuf al-Fihri's governors; no page dates any of it. The Abd al-Rahman I page: Yusuf was beaten at al-Musarah outside Córdoba, fled to Toledo and was killed there, but 'most of central and northern al-Andalus' stayed outside the emir's rule, 'with large swathes remaining in the hands of' others 'until 779 (submission of Zaragoza)'. The Emirate page: the 'first unification of al-Andalus (including Toledo, Zaragoza, Pamplona, and Barcelona) ... still took more than twenty-five years to complete'. The Yusuf page dates al-Musarah 'just outside Córdoba in March 756' (the Abd al-Rahman I page has the reign from 14 May 756) and Yusuf's death 759. Bridged at confidence 1 on Cliopatria's shape; the centre and the north are soft until 779-783.
759: Narbonne capitulates to the Franks. 'Narbonne capitulated to the Christian Franks in 759'; Pepin the Short 'conquered Septimania in 759'.
760: Roussillon falls to the Franks. 'The region of Roussillon was taken by the Franks in 760.'

region.text: the Ebro valley around Zaragoza that Cliopatria draws in the Frankish shape 778-782

ledger.note: 778: 53 cells of the Ebro valley around Zaragoza enter the Frankish shape. 'When Charlemagne invaded the Upper March in 778' (Septimania page). Cliopatria's reading, kept so that this dossier and kingdom-of-the-franks /ledger/59 and /65 (also confidence 1) name the same owner for the same cells; the Abd al-Rahman I page has Sulayman al-Arabi refuse the Franks entry to Zaragoza, and the Charlemagne expedition failed, so no Frankish rule there is documented.

region.text: the Upper March (Zaragoza, Huesca and Lleida): the 57 cells Cliopatria removes in 778 that are not in the Frankish shape

ledger.counterpart: rebellious lords of the Upper March
ledger.note: 778: the rest of the Upper March slips away as Charlemagne invades. 'When Charlemagne invaded the Upper March in 778'; the rebellious lords of Zaragoza (Sulayman al-Arabi, then al-Husayn) had invited him (Navarre page) and keep the land when the Franks leave. The emir's authority there returns by 783. [Repair eu-12-a, 2026-10-25: the 53 cells that Cliopatria gives the Franks are a separate event with kingdom-of-the-franks as counterpart.]

region.text: the Ebro valley cells that leave the Frankish shape in 783

ledger.note: 783: the 53 Ebro cells leave the Frankish shape again (kingdom-of-the-franks /ledger/65, confidence 1). 'By 783 Abd al-Rahman's army advanced on Zaragoza' (Abd al-Rahman I page).

region.text: the Upper March: the 57 cells that return in 783 and are not in the Frankish shape

ledger.counterpart: rebellious lords of the Upper March
ledger.note: 783: the emir's army marches on Zaragoza. 'By 783 Abd al-Rahman's army advanced on Zaragoza'; the page also has al-Husayn declare independence in 781 and, elsewhere, Zaragoza submit in 779, so the year is the shape's.

region.text: the county of Girona with Besalú

ledger.note: 785: Girona falls to the Franks. 'In 785 the county of Girona (with Besalú) to the south of the Pyrenees was taken.'

region.text: Urgell and Cerdanya, the Pyrenean valleys added to the Frankish march

ledger.note: 798: Urgell and Cerdanya pass to the Franks. 'Urgell and Cerdanya were added in 798.' The land is the cells Cliopatria removes between 793 and 800.
801: Louis the Pious takes Barcelona. 'Louis the Pious took Barcelona from its Moorish ruler in 801.'

region.text: the Navarre and Huesca belt under Frankish protection

ledger.note: 806: the Franks take Navarre under their protection. 'In 806 took Navarre under their protection' (Navarre page); the upper Ebro came under Frankish overlordship in 794 and Pamplona in 798 (Spanish March page). The land is the belt in Navarre and Huesca that Cliopatria removes in 806.

825: the Duero fringe leaves the shape as Asturias begins to resettle it. The Alfonso II page: after the 825 victories 'the repopulation of parts of Galicia, León, and Castile was started'; the page is silent on any Cordoban loss, so this bridges Cliopatria's five-cell change.

region.text: Toledo, the province and city that rose in 852

ledger.note: 852: Toledo rises again. 'In 852, a new revolt broke out in Toledo'; the governor was taken hostage and Emir Muhammad I's army was defeated in the reprisal; Toledo allied with Ordoño I of Asturias and lost at the Battle of Guadacelete. The page counts 'numerous insurrections' from 761 to 857; the city stays inside the emirate's Cliopatria shape, so this is drawn as a contest, not a loss.

region.text: Toledo, the province and city, where the truce of 859 ended the revolt

ledger.note: 859: truce with Toledo. 'In 859, Muhammad I negotiated a truce with Toledo.' The page then has the city 'virtually independent for twenty years' and Córdoba re-asserting control in 873 (its own dates do not agree), and the Banu Qasi with 'nominal control of Toledo until 920'; none of that is drawn, and the lords of Toledo have no dossier.
868: Porto falls to Asturias. 'Count Vimara Perez in 868 conquered Porto and resettled the district' (the page also says 867).

872: Furtun ibn Musa occupies Tudela. 'Furtun ibn Musa occupied Tudela, whose governor the Banu Qasi imprisoned at Arnedo, then killed following an escape.' The sentence carries no year of its own and stands in the page's passage on 872. Tudela stays Banu Qasi land until the vassalage of 898 and their removal in 924.

January 872: the sons of Musa ibn Musa take Zaragoza and Monzón. 'In January 872, Isma'il ibn Musa entered Zaragoza, and was there joined by Lubb, the two of them together taking Monzon.' The emirate's Cliopatria shapes 870-883 still draw Zaragoza; the emir takes it back in 884 (below). banu-qasi /ledger/0 founds the Banu Qasi state on this land. Zaragoza is read as its province.
878: Viseu and Lamego are resettled by Asturias. 'Christian forces repopulate Braga, Viseu, and Lamego.'

region.text: Coimbra and the land up to the Mondego

ledger.note: 879: Coimbra falls to Alfonso III. 'Conquered Porto and Coimbra in 867 and 879 respectively.'

883: Umar ibn Hafsun leads the rebel south. 'By 883, he had become the leader of the rebels in the provinces to the south and the west'; he held Reyyo (with Bobastro), Elvira (Granada) and Jaén (Abdallah page). The rebels hold the land until 913-928.

884: the emir takes Zaragoza. 'In 884 the emir sent two military campaigns into the region and took Zaragoza.' In 886 the new emir gave it to the rival Tujibids. The emir had lost Zaragoza to the Banu Qasi in January 872. [Repair eu-12-a, 2026-10-25]
898: the Banu Qasi submit for Tudela and Tarazona. Lubb ibn Muhammad 'recognizes Emir Abd Allah in exchange for the governorship of Tudela and Tarazona'.

region.text: everything beyond the vicinity of Córdoba, held by rebels and local lords

ledger.note: c. 900 (entered at 898, the year of the Banu Qasi submission and of Cliopatria's shape change): the emir's power shrinks to Córdoba. 'The power of emir Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Umawi (c. 900) did not extend beyond Córdoba itself'; at his death in 912 it did not extend 'not far beyond the vicinity of Córdoba' (Abd al-Rahman III page). The radius is a reading. [Repair eu-12-a, 2026-10-25: dated 898 so that the ledger and keyframe 898-910 agree; the page's own date is c. 900.]

903: the Balearic Islands are taken. 'In 903, the Muslims under the Arab Commander Issam al-Khawlani defeated the Franks and captured the Balearic Islands.' The islands had submitted to an Umayyad fleet in 707 and kept autonomy.

913: Écija and Seville return. 'On 1 January 913 an army, led by the eunuch Badr, conquered the fortress of Écija'; 'Seville finally capitulated on 20 December 913.' The page speaks of 'the rivalries between the Banu Hajjaj lords of Seville and Carmona'; it does not itself call the lord of Seville a Banu Hajjaj. [Repair eu-12-a: counterpart named for the lords the page names.]

region.text: the Hafsunid provinces except Bobastro, and Algeciras

ledger.note: 914: the rebel coast falls. The army reached Algeciras on 1 June 914 'after taking Málaga'; 'by the end of 914, he had captured 70 of Ibn Hafsun's castles' (Ibn Hafsun page). Bobastro itself holds out until 928.
915: Valencia submits. 'Valencia: the region submitted peacefully.'

ledger.counterpart: Banu Muhallab of Guadix and the lords of Jerez and Cádiz
ledger.note: 921: Guadix, Jerez and Cádiz submit. 'In 921 the Banu Muhallab of Guadix submitted,' followed by Jerez and Cádiz.

region.text: Pechina (Almería) and, undated, the rest of al-Andalus not held out by Toledo, Badajoz and the Upper March

ledger.note: 922: Pechina submits; Umayyad power is restored 'throughout al-Andalus' except Toledo, Badajoz and the Upper March. Pechina (Almería) is dated 922; the rest of the shape is the undated 'Abd al-Rahman III rapidly restored Umayyad power throughout al-Andalus' (Emirate page, not this one) and is bridged here. [Reviewer eu-12-a, 2026-10-25: confidence 2 to 1, as keyframe 18 already says; only Pechina is dated.]

924: the Banu Qasi are removed from Tudela. the Banu Qasi page: 'on his return to Tudela he removed the Banu Qasi and sent them to Córdoba' (the year after the fall of Viguera and Nájera in 923); the Tujibids take their place; 'The death of Muhammad ibn Lubb' in 929 ended them in the Ebro valley. [Reviewer eu-12-a, 2026-10-25: source changed from the Abd al-Rahman III page, which does not name Tudela.]
928: Bobastro surrenders. Hafs, the last of Ibn Hafsun's sons, 'surrendered in 928 and had his life spared' after a six-month siege; the Hafsunid rebellion ends.
929: Abd al-Rahman III proclaims the Caliphate of Córdoba. He declared himself caliph 'on 16 January 929'; the emirate becomes the caliphate (one state under a new title).

wars.name: Frankish conquest of Septimania
wars.outcome: Pepin the Short's expedition of 752 ends with the capitulation of Narbonne in 759 and the taking of Roussillon in 760; the Emirate keeps nothing north of the Pyrenees.
wars.note: The war begins under the Umayyad governors, four years before the Emirate (756).

wars.name: Abd al-Rahman I against Yusuf al-Fihri
wars.outcome: Abd al-Rahman beat Yusuf al-Fihri at al-Musarah 'just outside Córdoba in March 756'; Yusuf fled towards Toledo and died there, 759 in the infobox (one account: killed two or three years after the battle by his own men).
wars.note: The Abd al-Rahman I page: Yusuf raised a second army that the emir's governor at Seville defeated, and fled to Toledo; the head was sent to Córdoba. The dates of 756 differ between pages (March on the Yusuf page, reign from 14 May on the Abd al-Rahman I page). The Fihrid emirate of Ifriqiya in the fihrids dossier is a different branch.

wars.name: Abbasid expedition to al-Andalus
wars.outcome: Al-Ala ibn Mughith's Abbasid army is defeated at Carmona: 'By 763 Abd al-Rahman had to get back to the business of war.' No border moved.

wars.name: Charlemagne's Spanish expedition
belligerents: rebellious lords of the Upper March
wars.outcome: Invited by rebellious Muslim lords, Charlemagne failed before Zaragoza and his rearguard 'led by Roland was attacked by the Basque tribes' (Roncevaux, 15 August 778). The emir's army advanced on Zaragoza by 783.
wars.note: Dates of the Zaragoza revolt differ on the Abd al-Rahman I page (779 submission; 781 independence; 783 army). Cliopatria draws 53 Ebro cells in the Frankish shape 778-782 (confidence 1 here and in kingdom-of-the-franks); the pages opened do not put Frankish rule in Zaragoza.

wars.name: Frankish conquest of the Spanish March
wars.outcome: The Franks take Girona (785), Urgell and Cerdanya (798) and Barcelona (801); the Emirate's Pyrenean frontier falls back to the Llobregat and the Ebro.
wars.note: Cliopatria shows the losses in 788, 800 and 806.

wars.name: Battle of Pancorbo
wars.outcome: A Moorish victory over the Franks in 816 (Spanish March page); no border moved.

wars.name: Banu Qasi revolts and the Upper March
wars.outcome: Musa ibn Musa revolts with Íñigo Arista in the 840s; 859 Ordoño I and García Íñiguez defeat him; the emir takes Zaragoza in 884; Lubb submits in 898; Abd al-Rahman III removes the Banu Qasi from Tudela in 924.
wars.note: The 920 campaign 'in 920 the emir personally led the Cordoban army north'.

wars.name: Revolt of Toledo
wars.outcome: A new revolt broke out in Toledo in 852; Muhammad I's army was defeated in the reprisal; Toledo allied with Ordoño I of Asturias and lost at the Battle of Guadacelete; in 859 Muhammad I negotiated a truce.
wars.note: The page counts numerous insurrections from 761 to 857; only the 852 revolt and the 859 truce are dated.

wars.name: Asturian-Cordoban war of Alfonso III
wars.outcome: 'Fighting occurred almost constantly between 875 and 883'; Asturias gains the land between the Douro and the Mondego; peace in 884.

wars.name: Revolt of Umar ibn Hafsun
wars.outcome: The rebellion holds the south from 883; Ibn Hafsun is beaten near Polei in 891 (but 'reconquered all the lost territories' by 892), converts to Christianity in 899, makes peace in 911, dies in 917; Abd al-Rahman III takes the coast in 914 and Bobastro in 928.
wars.note: Abdallah page: 'In 911, the emir signed a peace agreement with Ibn Hafsun'.

wars.name: Reconquest of al-Andalus by Abd al-Rahman III

zones.text: Écija, Seville, Algeciras, Valencia, Guadix, Jerez, Cádiz, Pechina

wars.outcome: Écija and Seville (913), the coast to Algeciras (914), Valencia (915), Guadix, Jerez and Cádiz (921) and Pechina (922) return; Badajoz (930), Toledo (932) and Zaragoza (937) come after the emirate.

wars.name: Campaigns of 920 and 924 against León and Pamplona

zones.text: Osma and San Esteban de Gormaz

wars.outcome: In 920 Abd al-Rahman III 'captured the forts of Osma and San Esteban de Gormaz' (the page does not say whether they were garrisoned or kept, nor that León retook them), beat Navarre and León at Valdejunquera on 26 July and sacked Pamplona; in 924 he devastated Basque territory in a counter-offensive against Sancho Ordóñez of Navarre. No holding is recorded, so the ledger enters no gain for the two forts.
wars.note: Cliopatria draws no Cordoban gain on the Duero after 920. [Repair eu-12-a, 2026-10-25: reviewer finding (ledger had no gain for Osma and San Esteban): the alternative 'say none was held' taken, because the page is silent on holding; a 920 gain from kingdom-of-leon would have to be a guess.]

certainty.note: No treaty line is recorded in the pages opened: the Pyrenean frontier of the Spanish March, the Duero belt and the Upper March are approximate; from c. 900 to 922 the emirate is the vicinity of Córdoba with nominal overlordship beyond.

sources.title: Emirate of Córdoba

notes:
Cliopatria rows: shapes 898 to 926 draw the whole of al-Andalus although the Emirate page says the emir's power c. 900 'did not extend beyond Córdoba itself'; the dossier shrinks the emirate to the vicinity of Córdoba (radius 90 km, a reading) with the Balearics (903) and the Banu Qasi march as a vassal, then adds the dated reconquests of 913-922. The 922 and 926 shapes omit Toledo, Badajoz and the Upper March (dated 932, 930, 937 by the Abd al-Rahman III page). 757 holds Septimania until 759; the 930-935 years of the 926 shape belong to the caliphate-of-cordoba dossier. Emirate and Caliphate are one Umayyad state: treat 929 as a rename (the caliphate-of-cordoba agent is another group). Mérida, Toledo's rebellions of the 9th century and Pamplona's alliance with Córdoba are not on the pages opened. Counterparts written here by eu-12-a: banu-qasi (Zaragoza, Tudela; Cliopatria lacks it) and the rebel state rebellion-of-umar-ibn-hafsun; still needing dossiers: Tujibids of Zaragoza, the Banu Hajjaj of Seville and the lords of Toledo, Badajoz (Ibn Marwan) and Mérida. Page conflicts: Zaragoza 779 or 781-783 (Abd al-Rahman I page); Porto 867 or 868; Lisbon 797 or 798. Pages budget: 9 pages opened for this state, plus Navarre, Alfonso II and III pages already opened for the Asturias dossier. Gazetteer names used that do not exist: none (coordinates are used for Guadix, Algeciras, Bobastro, Tudela–Tarazona, Osma). Names needed: Urgell, Cerdanya, Upper March, Reyyo, Elvira, Bobastro, Tudela, Tarazona, Guadix, Pechina.

Repairs 2026-10-25 (eu-12-a, after the adversarial review): ledger 757 gain from the Fihrid governors (confidence 1; Yusuf al-Fihri war added); 778 and 783 split so the 53 Ebro cells Cliopatria gives the Franks mirror kingdom-of-the-franks /ledger/59 and /65, the rest stays with the rebellious lords of the Upper March; January 872 losses of Zaragoza with Monzón and of Tudela to the Banu Qasi, keyframes 870, 875 and 878 now adjust; Girona out of keyframe 783 from 785; the c. 900 collapse entered at 898 with the c. noted; counterparts Fihrid governors of al-Andalus, rebellious lords of the Upper March, Banu Hajjaj of Seville, autonomous lords of al-Andalus, Banu Muhallab of Guadix and the lords of Jerez and Cádiz, and lords of Toledo are listed as needing dossiers; Toledo's revolt of 852 and truce of 859 added from the Toledo page (the 761-857 insurrections are otherwise undated; Mérida's page dates no revolt, only the Alcazaba of 835, so Mérida stays a gap). Osma and San Esteban de Gormaz (920): the Abd al-Rahman III page says the forts were captured and is silent on whether they were held, so no gain is entered. Alfonso II page re-read for the 825 Duero fringe: it names no Duero town and no gain from Córdoba ('repopulation of parts of Galicia, León, and Castile was started'; Lisbon 'captured and sacked' in 798), so ledger 825 stays at confidence 1. Disagreement: none with the reviewer; the 757 gain is a bridge, because the Abd al-Rahman I page says most of central and northern al-Andalus stayed outside the emir's rule until 779, which Cliopatria's 757 shape does not show.
